# Phyllum

> A design system companion that turns prose, images, or the styles already in a codebase into named tokens and components, all recorded in one file.

Phyllum writes exactly one file in a user's codebase: `DESIGN-SYSTEM.md`, plus a
`DESIGN-SYSTEM.md.bak` holding the state one edit ago, plus its own gitignored
`.phyllum/` — and, only when you name one on the command line, the `.json` file
`assess --json` writes. Every command is rerunnable and converges — re-assessing doesn't
duplicate tokens, re-creating a component opens a revision. `assess` reads the codebase,
`tokenise` reads a sentence, `create` reads intent, and `apply` plans getting the recorded
system into the code — writing a reviewable PRD to `.phyllum/PRD.md` and executing none of
it — and `update` is the editing verb, changing a token or component the design system
already records; moving the install is `upgrade`. `apply run` is the single exception to the write rule: it executes that plan on a
`phyllum/apply-<date>` branch of its own, one commit per phase, writing only the files the
running phase's criteria name. Mechanical commands run in pure Node; the intelligent ones
(`create`, `tokenise`) run natively inside a Claude Code session or shell out to the
`claude` CLI — with one exception inside `create`: `create primitives` is wholly
mechanical, shipped constants and deterministic arithmetic, so it needs no model.
Phyllum's naming vocabulary and its ramp constants are shipped as parsed spec tables in
`skill/refs/`, never as code and never as an npm dependency; the zero-dependency rule is
absolute.
These paths are repo-relative. Phyllum is published on npm as `phyllum`; the source lives at https://github.com/ndisisnd/phyllum.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): what Phyllum is, how to install it, how it works
- [Skill definition](skill/SKILL.md): the router — commands, the file format, the two rules that outrank being helpful. Start here to change behaviour.
- [CLI entry point](bin/phyllum.js): argument parsing and the single call into execute; the terminal surface
- [File template](templates/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md): the canonical DESIGN-SYSTEM.md skeleton every install scaffolds

## Reference

- [create](skill/refs/create.md): the three modes (prose, image, pick), the fifteen archetype contracts, custom mode — no contract, no gap list, recorded exactly as described and marked as such — the follow-up loop, acceptance and the write step, plus `create primitives` — primitive colour ramps, asked per token, written under Colours' `Primitives` subsection
- [assess](skill/refs/assess.md): the read-only codebase scan — what is read (text files in any language, bounded: build output, dependency directories, gitignored paths, oversized files and non-text files are skipped), React-only component detection, clustering before naming, the diff on rerun, and the judgement half: severities on every finding, similarity groups scored into clone/similar bands, naming drift and prop mismatches, hygiene (framework collisions, unused tokens and components), and the drift score and verdict the run ends in; `--json [path]` writes the whole assessment to one file instead of reviewing it
- [apply](skill/refs/apply.md): planning the design system into the code and then executing that plan — harness detection and its precedence, one acceptance criterion per change, one phase per commit, the PRD's marker contract, resume vs `--fresh`, and for `apply run`: the harness hand-off, the branch and commit guarantees, the mechanical-vs-agent split, `.phyllum/config.json`'s model overrides, per-phase verification, and the source-write grant
- [tokenise](skill/refs/tokenise.md): naming the values in one sentence — the proposal queue and its splitting grammar (several values in one sentence, one question at a time, in sentence order, duplicates collapsed, a skip costing only itself), the three passes, every colour format read alike (`#2563EB`, `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`, `hsl()`, `#rrggbbaa`) with values compared by channel — alpha included, so two alphas are two facts — and recorded exactly as typed, gradients as a colour value (the six `*-gradient()` shapes, recorded verbatim, written into Colours, every proposed name carrying the word `gradient` and `gradient-{n}` as the fallback scale), the kind picker an empty run opens (colour / typography / border radius / spacing / something else, with the solid-or-gradient fork under colour and the prose each pick builds), the argument hint every value question wears, the naming sources (the nomenclature library first where the sentence signals a role, the lightness/saturation scales as fallback), the follow-up loop, acceptance
- [init](skill/refs/init.md): the guided setup walkthrough — scaffold, skill install, optional seeding
- [nomenclature](skill/refs/nomenclature.md): the shared library no command owns — the standard token-naming vocabulary (four slots in a fixed order, a strict word list per slot: families, ranks, exception words, state words), the nine shipped neutral-ramp constants, and the fixed lightness-and-saturation scale a derived ramp is placed on. Read by `tokenise`'s name suggestions and by `create primitives`; it is data, not behaviour, and nothing in it runs on its own
- [gui](skill/refs/gui.md): the localhost server contract and the three-view dashboard, plus the presentation contract — colour tokens as cards in a responsive grid (a rounded swatch on top, the name and then the value beneath it), near-white swatches bordered, gradients painted as the swatch fill and only a value the page recognises ever inlined into a style attribute, primitives ramps keeping their nine-step strips, typography as live specimens, numbers as measured bars; hand-written Carbon-like styling with no dependency and no network fetch, read-only as ever
- [display](skill/refs/system.md): the terminal listing format; `system` is the same command under its older name, kept as a permanent alias
- [version](skill/refs/version.md): the installed version, the on-demand npm registry check, and what happens offline
- [upgrade](skill/refs/upgrade.md): moving the install to the latest published version — install detection (npm/pnpm, global/project), the graceful refusals, and the skill re-sync
- [update](skill/refs/update.md): the editing verb from v0.4.0 — the menu and its one 0.4.x `apply` breadcrumb, the `component`/`token` chains, prose target-matching (exact names resolve, anything else is asked about rather than guessed), the token flow (type → the full list of that section → pick → a sentence), the rename ripple over every spec slot and Backlog line, the convergence re-check on a new value, `update component` riding `create`'s own revision machinery, and the never-list: no codebase, no PRD, nothing written before the gate, no invented or corrected value, no deletion. It stopped being `apply`'s alias in this release, and `apply` carries no alias at all now
